extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, academics, students, scientific instrument purchasers, and applicants for academic posts
extracted.subtask_short: submitting letters and adverts to Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural requirements for submitting letters and advertisements to the journal Nature (addresses, rates, formatting rules, payment) as published in the July 1907 supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHAIR OF NATURAL HISTORY — application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governing Body invite applications for the Chair of Natural History (Geology, Botany, Zoology) to become vacant. Salary about £175 per annum, with house and residence in College. Candidates, with statement of age, qualifications, experience, and original testimonials, to be addressed to the Principal on or before (date given). The Professor will be required to enter upon his duties on October 8 next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particulars on application to the College. Applications must include statement of age, qualifications, experience, and original testimonials; address applications to the Principal by the advertised deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic appointment applications — include references and meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for posts (e.g., Assistant Lecturer and Demonstrator in Zoology, University of Manchester) should be forwarded together with the name of at least one reference by a stated date (example: by July 17) to the Registrar or address given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each advertisement's instructions: include required particulars, at least one referee name where requested, and send to the named official (Registrar/Principal) by the deadline specified to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting letters to Nature — address and editorial addressee
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters for Nature should be addressed to the Publishers; the Editor's address for Nature is given as 'Physic,' London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send correspondence to the Publishers/Editor at the office (St. Martin's Street, London, W.C.) as instructed in the journal's notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges for advertisements in Nature — format and pricing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for advertisements are published (yearly, half-yearly, quarterly). Notable rule: 'The first line being in heavy type is charged for as Two Lines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad rates and column/page fractions are set in the published table; heavy first line counts as two lines for charging. Cheques and Money Orders payable to MACMILLAN & CO., Limited; follow office address and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becker's Anglemeter — measuring height of an accessible object (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: To measure the height of an accessible object (e.g., tall pole) set the pinhole to the angle marked 45°. Hold the Anglemeter in a vertical plane and sight a spot on the pole at the observer's eye level through the pinhole exactly over the line on the mirror. Pace backwards, keeping the pointer set at this angle, until you obtain the reflection of the top of the pole on the cross line in the mirror. When this occurs, the distance paced from the object to this spot equals the height of the top of the pole above the observer's eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single observation at 45° yields height equal to horizontal distance from observer to sighting spot; follow exact sighting procedure for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becker's Anglemeter — measuring height of an inaccessible object (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the object is inaccessible a second reading is necessary; a baseline must be measured and angles taken at each end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two-angle triangulation with a measured baseline when a single observation is impossible; measure baseline accurately and record both angles for height calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becker's Anglemeter — surveying angles between distant objects (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For surveying, sight the first object through the pinhole so its outer edge is exactly above the centre of the mirror, then slide the sight until the other point is observed in the mirror exactly on the scratch. Read the scale to obtain the angle between the two objects and the observer's eye (example: reading 65° gives an angular separation of 65°).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure gives immediate angular reading between two points; useful for making maps and for teaching practical surveying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becker's Anglemeter — accuracy and practice recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anglemeter allows readings to one-fifth of a degree. It is recommended to practise with objects not too far distant and not too small. In practice surveys made with the Anglemeter can be as accurate as with a chain, and the instrument avoids difficulties from inequalities of the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with nearer, larger objects to gain familiarity; the instrument is presented as suitable for teaching Mathematics, Practical Geography, and Surveying; testimonials from practitioners and professors are cited to support utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: University vacation course entries — deadline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Vacation courses (e.g., University College: Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Physiology and Anatomy for medical students) require entries to be sent to the undersigned on or before August 15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send entries by the stated deadline to be enrolled; fees and further particulars available from the named secretary/office.
